facts: *The Gambler* is a novel by Fyodor Dostoyevsky.
The eBook edition was originally released on May 1, 2000.
The text was most recently updated on July 1, 2020.
The eBook is organized into seventeen chapters.
The narrator returns to Roulettenberg after a two-week absence.
Polina expresses frustration at receiving only 700 gülden from pledged diamonds.
The narrator quarrels with a French Marquis over Russian mistreatment at European tables d'hôte.
Polina reveals that the family awaits news of their grandmother's death in St. Petersburg.
The narrator enters a casino for the first time.
He wins 1,600 gülden while playing with Polina's money.
Polina insists that they become gambling partners and share profits equally.
The General warned the narrator that gambling would compromise him.
The narrator has a complex relationship with Polina.
The General is waiting for news from St. Petersburg about his mother.
Mlle. Blanche is a wealthy Frenchwoman with a questionable background.
Mr. Astley warns the narrator about Mlle. Blanche's character.
The narrator played roulette with six hundred gülden belonging to Polina Alexandrovna.
He initially won approximately 4,000 gülden before losing everything in two large bets.
The narrator claimed the gambling money was his own capital during lunch.
The General dismissed the narrator as an insufferable charlatan.
The narrator confronts Polina about the Marquis de Griers's absence.
Polina reveals she is in debt and needs to win at gambling.
The narrator confesses his obsessive love for Polina.
The narrator accepts a challenge to compliment the Baroness Burmergelm.
The narrator insulted Baron and Baroness Burmergelm on a carriage path.
The General promised the narrator's dismissal from the household.
The narrator threatened to challenge the Baron himself.
Maria Philipovna has mysteriously departed to Carlsbad.
The narrator has 160 gülden remaining.
De Griers is sent by the General to dissuade the narrator from confronting the Baron.
The narrator plans to recruit Mr. Astley as his second for a meeting with the Baron.
Polina urges the narrator to abandon his plans in a note.
The narrator confesses his love for Polina at a café.
Mlle. Blanche de Cominges was expelled from Roulettenberg three years ago.
Blanche seeks to marry the General to escape her disreputable history.
A woman calls out "Alexis Ivanovitch" from the verandah as the narrator walks toward his hotel.
Antonida Vassilievna Tarassevitcha is seventy-five years old.
She arrived at a luxury spa hotel carried in an armchair.
The General believed Antonida was gravely ill before her arrival.
Antonida criticized the General for his financial mismanagement.
The Grandmother is mistakenly registered as a princess at the spa.
She wins 4,200 gülden by betting on zero at the roulette wheel.
Her total winnings accumulate to 12,000 florins.
She instructs Alexis Ivanovitch to take her home after collecting her money.
The elderly Russian grandmother wins twelve thousand florins at roulette.
She refuses to give any money to her heir, the General.
Alexis Ivanovitch is asked to deliver a letter to Mr. Astley.
The grandmother commands Alexis to return to the casino at four o'clock.
The Grandmother loses approximately 15,000 roubles at Roulettenberg Casino.
She gambles through the night with a Polish stranger and loses roughly ten thousand roubles.
The Grandmother gives the narrator five hundred gülden before dismissing him.
Polina declines the Grandmother's invitation to join her, hinting at a romantic involvement with De Griers.
The Grandmother loses nearly one hundred thousand roubles at the Casino.
The Grandmother departs by the 9:30 train after borrowing three thousand francs from Mr. Astley.
Mlle. Blanche abandons the General upon learning of his financial ruin.
The narrator finds Polina waiting for him by the window after escorting the Grandmother to the station.
Polina arrives at the narrator's hotel room with a letter from De Griers.
The narrator suggests consulting Mr. Astley to solve their financial problems.
The narrator wins one hundred thousand florins at the casino.
The narrator returns to his hotel room and shows his winnings to Polina.
The narrator wins 200,000 francs at roulette.
The narrator offers 50,000 francs to Polina to pay off her debt to De Griers.
Polina throws the money in the narrator's face and flees.
The narrator departs for Paris with Mlle. Blanche and her mother.
The narrator spends 200,000 francs during his stay in Paris.
Mlle. Blanche extracts 100,000 francs in cash from the narrator.
Blanche marries the General to secure her status and access to wealth.
The narrator leaves Paris with five hundred francs and personal effects.
The narrator has lost money gambling for eighteen months.
The narrator meets his old friend Mr. Astley in Homburg.
Polina, a woman the narrator cares for, is traveling in Switzerland.
The narrator has fifteen louis d'or remaining.
